hypotheses.text: Heterozygous RAB3A switch II missense variants (specifically p.Arg83Trp) cause an adult-onset, slowly progressive cerebellar ataxia syndrome with mild spasticity and action tremor, rather than an exclusively congenital or infantile non-progressive ataxic encephalopathy.
hypotheses.rationale: Prior binned assertions highlighted early-onset or infantile-onset hypotonia and ataxia; however, the primary characterization of the index SCA52 kindreds (Families T and K) by Miyamoto et al. demonstrates adult-onset progressive cerebellar disease with pyramidal signs (mild spasticity) and tremors, indicating phenotypic heterogeneity or variant-specific age of onset.

evidence.text: Miyamoto et al. identified the c.247C>T p.(Arg83Trp) variant in RAB3A in two families with cerebellar ataxia where affected individuals presented with adult-onset, gradually progressive cerebellar symptoms, often accompanied by mild gait spasticity and tremors, alongside cerebellar atrophy accentuated in the vermis.

hypotheses.text: Extraneurological organ involvement (specifically cardiomyopathy, visual failure from optic atrophy or retinopathy, and hepatic dysfunction) is completely absent (0/N) in all genetically confirmed heterozygous RAB3A-related SCA52 index cases.
hypotheses.rationale: Testing whether non-ataxia systemic features are universally absent across index pedigrees is critical to distinguishing SCA52 from mitochondrial, metabolic, and complex multisystem spinocerebellar degenerations.

evidence.text: Primary clinicopathological investigation of RAB3A p.Arg83Trp families showed selective cerebellar cortical degeneration and variable neurodevelopmental symptoms without reported cardiac, retinal, or systemic organ dysfunction.

source.title: An R83W mutation in Rab3A causes autosomal-dominant cerebellar ataxia
source.quote: Brain MRI consistently revealed cerebellar atrophy, often accentuated in the vermis, and neuropathological examinations demonstrated diffuse cerebellar cortical degeneration.

hypotheses.text: Cerebellar vermian atrophy on neuroimaging is a fully penetrant (100%) invariant imaging biomarker in symptomatic RAB3A-associated ataxia individuals.
hypotheses.rationale: Establishing whether vermis-accentuated cerebellar atrophy is obligatory across all reported symptomatic carriers establishes a strong negative rule-out criterion (i.e. normal cerebellar volume in symptomatic adults rules out SCA52).

evidence.text: Brain magnetic resonance imaging consistently demonstrated cerebellar atrophy accentuated in the vermis in all examined affected carriers across the index families.

new_directions.question_text: What exact clinical numerator and denominator frequencies of pyramidal spasticity, tremor, and intellectual disability were documented across each affected member of Family T and Family K in Miyamoto et al. (2026)?
new_directions.rationale: Direct extraction of individual pedigree charts from Miyamoto et al. will yield precise phenotypic numerators/denominators for dysarthria, spasticity, tremors, and cognitive delay in human RAB3A disease.

new_directions.question_text: Does the phenotypic spectrum of dominant RAB3A mutations overlap with downstream or upstream regulators in the exocytosis pathway (such as RIM1 or RAB3GAP1) regarding the presence of peripheral neuropathy or ocular defects?
new_directions.rationale: Comparing RAB3GAP1 phenotypes (which exhibit ocular abnormalities and severe peripheral neuropathy in humans and canine models) against RAB3A cases will clarify whether exocytic GTPase machinery mutations selectively spare the peripheral nervous system in dominant human SCA52.
